original_question: Is the positive strong polarized relation for the pseudointersection number p exactly equivalent to p < s? In other words, does \( inom{p}{\omega} 	o  inom{p}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) hold if and only if p is strictly less than the splitting number s?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.18 in Section 2 (Countable problems) of the 17-page arXiv v2/preprint; its notation is fixed by Definition 0.1 and its forward implication is motivated by Theorem 1.6.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the exact open problem almost verbatim: it uses the right pair (\mathfrak{p},\omega), the right two-color strong polarized relation \binom{\mathfrak{p}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{p}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2, and the right biconditional with the strict inequality \mathfrak{p}<\mathfrak{s}. It also stays on the paper's intended comparison between the pseudointersection number and the splitting number, rather than drifting to neighboring invariants.
missing_details: Replace plain p and s by the standard cardinal-invariant notation \mathfrak{p} and \mathfrak{s}.
Say explicitly that \mathfrak{p} is the pseudointersection number and \mathfrak{s} is the splitting number on \omega.

Define the arrow notation: for every coloring c:\mathfrak{p}\times\omega\to 2, there should exist A\subseteq\mathfrak{p} and B\subseteq\omega with |A|=\mathfrak{p}, |B|=\omega, and c restricted to A\times B constant.
Make clear that the question is asked as a ZFC truth question, not merely as a consistency question.
Indicate that the relation in question is the two-color strong polarized relation for the pair (\mathfrak{p},\omega).

For paper-faithful context, note that the direction \mathfrak{p}<\mathfrak{s} \Rightarrow \binom{\mathfrak{p}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{p}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 is already supplied in the paper via Theorem 1.6; the real open content is whether the converse holds.
refined_question: In ZFC, let \mathfrak{p} and \mathfrak{s} denote the pseudointersection number and the splitting number on \omega. Is the two-color strong polarized relation \binom{\mathfrak{p}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{p}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 equivalent to \mathfrak{p}<\mathfrak{s}; that is, is it true that every coloring c:\mathfrak{p}\times\omega\to 2 admits A\subseteq\mathfrak{p} and B\subseteq\omega with |A|=\mathfrak{p}, |B|=\omega, and c restricted to A\times B constant if and only if \mathfrak{p}<\mathfrak{s}?
justification: The draft matches the paper's official target almost exactly: the accessible arXiv v2/preprint states this as Problem 2.18. The surrounding paragraph first notes a weaker polarized relation below \mathfrak{p}, then explicitly says that by Theorem 1.6, \mathfrak{p}<\mathfrak{s} yields the positive relation, and then asks whether the full biconditional holds. Definition 0.1 gives the exact meaning of the strong polarized arrow notation. I therefore kept the question narrowly on that equivalence and only made explicit the definitions and quantifiers needed to make it stand alone.
